title: Urinary catheter placement
what: A thin, soft tube is passed through the urethra into the bladder so urine drains into a bag.
why: When you cannot pass urine on your own, during and after surgery, to measure urine exactly, or for some illnesses.
duration: placing it usually takes 5 to 10 minutes; the catheter stays in from a few hours to a few weeks
tell_doctor: Allergy to latex or numbing gel
Prostate problems, a narrowed urethra, or urinary tract surgery
If placing a catheter was hard before

prepare.title: Hygiene
prepare.text: If you can, wash your genital area beforehand. The nurse will clean the skin anyway.

prepare.title: Feeling ready
prepare.text: Ask what the nurse is going to do. You can ask for a screen.

bring: If you go home with the catheter: your questions for the nurse about the bag and care
steps: You lie on your back with your legs slightly apart
The skin around the area is cleaned with antiseptic
A numbing gel is put into the urethra
The tube is slowly moved up into the bladder
When urine starts to flow, a small balloon inside is filled. It holds the catheter in place
The tube is connected to a bag and taped to your leg
feel: Burning and pressure as the tube goes in
An urge to pee. This is normal and usually passes
after: Keep the bag below your bladder, and do not put it on the floor
Drink enough water, unless your doctor limited it
Do not pull on the tube, and make sure it is not kinked
Wash the skin around the catheter with soap every day
When the catheter is removed, the balloon is emptied first. It is quick
For a while after removal, peeing may burn a little
red_flags: No urine in the bag for several hours, and your lower belly feels full and tight
Blood or clots in the urine
The catheter fell out, or severe pain in the lower belly

faq.q: Does putting in a urinary catheter hurt?
faq.a: Usually it is uncomfortable but bearable, because a numbing gel is used. Most people feel burning and an urge to pee.

faq.q: Why do I keep feeling I need the toilet with a catheter?
faq.a: The balloon irritates the bladder. It usually passes. If it does not, tell your doctor.
